channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Dino autoriza acesso da PF à investigação sobre produtora do 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino authorized the Federal Police to access data from the investigation led by the São Paulo Civil Police into the production company behind 'Dark Horse', a biopic about former president Jair Bolsonaro. The decision responds to a request from the Federal Police to monitor the case, which involves inquiries about the production of the film.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro endossa crítica a Michelle e reacende tensão na família durante campanha
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro used his social media to endorse criticism against Michelle Bolsonaro, reigniting internal divisions within former president Jair Bolsonaro's family during the election campaign. The episode comes as Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tries to strengthen his candidacy, exposing the fragility of family unity as a political strategy. The move highlights latent tensions that could impact right-wing coordination ahead of 2026.

item.title: Vídeo: Senado Verifica: saiba como os candidatos podem usar a IA nas eleições
item.description: Senado Verifica produced a video explaining how candidates and parties can use artificial intelligence in the 2026 elections. The report, presented by Paula Oda, addresses the limits and possibilities of using this technology in the Brazilian electoral context.

item.title: Candidatos são obrigados a participar de debates eleitorais? Entenda as regras
item.description: Brazilian electoral law does not require candidates to attend debates; the obligation falls on broadcasters, which must invite parties with at least five members in Congress. The absences of Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema from the Band debate drew criticism from opponents like Ronaldo Caiado, who backed a bill to make participation mandatory.

item.title: Candidato do Psol aciona MPE contra Renan Santos por fala sobre Janja
item.description: Olímpio Rocha (Psol), a candidate for governor of Paraíba, filed a complaint with the Electoral Public Ministry (MPE) against presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) over statements made about first lady Janja during the Band presidential debate. The complaint seeks investigation for electoral injury and violation of Article 243 of the Electoral Code, citing Law 14.192/2021 on political violence against women. It requests preservation of the debate footage and social media content for the electoral authority's analysis.

item.title: Lula x Bolsonaro: relembre o que diziam as pesquisas em agosto de 2022
item.description: CartaCapital revisits August 2022 polls that showed Lula far ahead of Bolsonaro (up to 15 points in Datafolha), before the PT candidate won the first round with 48.4% against 43.2%. Four years later, a new Nexus/BTG Pactual survey shows a technical tie between Lula (41%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (37% in the first round; 46% to 45% in a runoff), within a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Ao vivo: Poder360 entrevista Eduardo Girão
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo), the vice-presidential candidate running alongside Romeu Zema, will be interviewed live by Poder360 at 4 PM on Monday (Aug 24, 2026). Elected in 2018 from Ceará, he abandoned his gubernatorial bid to join Zema's presidential ticket. His main platforms include the defense of life from conception, anti-drug policies, and opposition to gambling and unrestricted access to firearms.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro aciona TSE contra Durigan por uso da máquina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) campaign filed a complaint with the TSE against Finance Minister Dario Durigan and President Lula, accusing them of prohibited conduct by public agents in the 2026 campaign. The filing, to be reviewed by Justice André Mendonça, alleges Durigan acted as an economic spokesperson for Lula's candidacy while holding office, citing his participation in a Santander event and a CBN interview. The campaign seeks investigation into who funded the agendas and whether federal structures were used for electoral benefit.

item.title: A avaliação da campanha de Augusto Cury sobre o primeiro debate presidencial
item.description: Augusto Cury's (Avante) campaign assessed his presidential debate debut on TV Bandeirantes positively, despite the absences of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema's last-minute withdrawal. The coordination highlighted the defense of the 'SUS da Mente' mental health policy and the psychiatrist's 'serene firmness' during exchanges with Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos.

item.title: A inércia da campanha é aliada de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with Lula leading by just one point in the runoff scenario (46% to 45%). The article emphasizes that beyond the numbers, the trend favors Flávio, who jumped from 36% to 45% while Lula moved only slightly from 41% to 46%, suggesting that the inertia of Lula's campaign is benefiting the PL candidate.

item.title: Leia a íntegra de nova pesquisa Nexus/BTG sobre a eleição para presidente
item.description: A Nexus/BTG Pactual poll released on August 24, 2026, shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) at 41% and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 37% in the first round, within a two-percentage-point margin of error. In the simulated second round, the race remains tight, with Lula at 46% and Flávio at 45%. The survey interviewed 2,006 voters by phone between August 21 and 23.

item.title: Lobista gastava R$ 100 mil por mês com casa usada por Lulinha, diz PF
item.description: Messages intercepted by the Federal Police (PF) show that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger spent R$ 100,000 per month maintaining a house used by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, the eldest son of President Lula. The conversations, dated 2025, indicate a financial arrangement between the lobbyist and the businessman, raising suspicions of undue favors and money laundering. The case may generate new developments in investigations involving people close to the president.

item.title: Filiado ao Psol aciona MPE contra Renan Santos por fala sobre Janja
item.description: A lawyer affiliated with the Psol party filed a complaint with the Electoral Public Ministry against presidential candidate Renan Santos of the Missão party for alleged electoral injury and misogyny. The complaint stems from statements made by Renan about First Lady Janja during Sunday's debate on the 23rd. The case will be reviewed by the MPE.

item.title: Lula associa fim da escala 6x1 a tempo com família em meio pressão sobre o Congresso
item.description: President Lula linked the end of the 6x1 work scale to more family time for workers. The move aims to pressure Congress to approve the bill reducing the workweek. The statement was made this Monday (24).

item.title: Caiado cita Poze e Oruam em defesa de educação contra o crime
item.description: Presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) linked public security and education policies during the launch of the Pacto Brasil de Futuro in São Paulo. He argued that fighting crime also requires preventing young people from being recruited by drug trafficking, citing MCs Poze and Oruam as examples.

item.title: Fomos ingênuos de achar que big techs eram neutras, diz Moraes
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes stated at the São Paulo Municipal Court of Accounts that it was naive to believe big techs are neutral companies, as they have ideology, economic and political purposes. He compared voters to consumers and candidates to products for sale, criticizing the use of algorithms to exploit frustrations of people who felt disadvantaged.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula sugere a Trump tomar trago com Putin e Xi Jinping
item.description: During a campaign rally in Minas Gerais, President Lula commented on the phone call he had with Donald Trump on August 22, also mentioning conversations with the leaders of China and Russia. According to Lula, he discussed the Ukraine war with Trump, Xi Jinping, and Putin, playfully suggesting the American leader share a drink with the others.

item.title: MPF investiga emenda de Eros Biondini (PL-MG) em esquema do INSS
item.description: Brazil's Federal Public Ministry (MPF) is investigating the allocation of a R$5 million parliamentary amendment from federal deputy Eros Biondini (PL-MG) to Instituto Terra e Trabalho (ITT), an entity linked to Conafer, which is under scrutiny for irregularities in INSS benefit charges. A Federal Police report indicates that Conafer transferred R$60,000 to the deputy's daughter, state deputy Chiara Biondini (PL-MG), in payments allegedly used to blackmail Eros. The lawmaker maintains there was no irregularity in his conduct and advocates for oversight of the funds.

item.title: Bolsonaro fez tudo para proteger o filho, Lula não faz “nada”, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, stated during a UOL and Folha sabatina that President Lula 'does nothing' to favor or harm investigations into his son Lulinha, contrasting this with former president Bolsonaro, who 'did everything to protect his son and friends.' Haddad pointed out that Lula has not replaced the Justice Minister, the Federal Police director, or the lead investigator as proof the investigations remain intact. He also defended the integrity of the investigative process and praised Minister André Mendonça's decision to investigate leaks related to the case.

item.title: Não foi só Kassab que dormiu no debate
item.description: The article criticizes absences in Brazilian presidential debates, noting that this year the problem was even worse than usual. It highlights that the polling frontrunner traditionally skips these events, and points to Kassab falling asleep during the debate, while emphasizing he was not the only one absent. The piece questions the relevance of debates in the era of short-form social media clips.

item.title: Lobista ameaçou parar de pagar passagens a Lulinha para bancar R$ 100 mil por mês em casa, aponta PF
item.description: The Federal Police suspect that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger spent around R$ 100,000 monthly maintaining a house used by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula. In a 2025 transcribed dialogue, Roberta threatened to cut off airfare payments to Lulinha to cover the property's expenses. The investigation involves businessman Cléber Ribas as a possible intermediary and takes place amid probes into INSS retirement fund diversion, with the case overseen by Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça.

item.title: Lula aceita convite de Erdoğan e deve ir à COP31 na Turquia
item.description: President Lula accepted Turkish President Recep Erdoğan's invitation to attend COP31 on Climate Change, to be held in Antalya, Turkey, in November 2026. During the phone call, both leaders announced the creation of a Strategic Council to deepen bilateral relations and celebrated the ratification of the Defense Industry Cooperation Agreement. Lula expressed interest in expanding defense investments and fostering partnerships between Brazilian and Turkish companies.

item.title: Fachin se reúne com Janja para discutir combate à violência de gênero
item.description: Brazil's Supreme Court Chief Justice Edson Fachin meets on Monday (Aug 24, 2026) with First Lady Janja Lula da Silva to discuss actions against gender-based violence, including the National Pact Against Feminicide. The meeting follows an STF ruling expanding the scope of protective measures under the Maria da Penha Law and comes amid record femicide numbers recorded in 2025.

item.title: Nova pesquisa presidencial testa disputa Lula x Flávio após debate da Band
item.description: Instituto Vox Brasil begins a new national presidential poll this Tuesday (25) with 2,100 interviews, following Sunday's (23) Band debate, with results scheduled for release on Saturday (29). The survey will test three second-round scenarios: Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro, Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, while also measuring first-round voting intentions, candidate rejection, Lula government approval, and the impact of the main candidates' absence from the debate, with a margin of error of 2.15 percentage points.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula participa de reunião do Contrata+Brasil
item.description: President Lula participated on Monday (Aug 24, 2026) in a meeting of Contrata+Brasil, a federal government platform focused on contracting small businesses. The event took place at the Palácio do Planalto at 3 PM, with the participation of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin. The initiative aims to expand small businesses' participation in public contracts, bringing entrepreneurs closer to opportunities offered by the government.

item.title: Mauro Mendes lidera com folga a disputa pelo Senado no MT
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas poll shows former governor Mauro Mendes (União Brasil) as the frontrunner for one of Mato Grosso's Senate seats in 2026, with 52.3% of voting intentions. State representative Janaina Riva (MDB) ranks second with 33.7%, also holding a comfortable lead over third-place José Medeiros (PL) at 18.8%. The survey interviewed 1,504 voters between August 21 and 23, with a margin of error of 2.6 percentage points.

item.title: Eleições 2026: como consultar o local de votação
item.description: Brazilian voters can check their polling location for the 2026 elections through the Electoral Justice self-service portal or the e-Título app, accessing details such as zone, section, and address. It is not mandatory to provide the voter registration number, as searches can be done by full name or CPF. The location may differ from previous elections due to transfers or registration changes.

item.title: PT vai à Justiça Eleitoral contra ônibus “fora Lula” de Ricardo Salles
item.description: The Desperta Brasil coalition, supporting Fernando Haddad's bid for the São Paulo government, filed a complaint with the TRE-SP requesting the removal of a branded bus used by Senate candidate Ricardo Salles (Novo). The vehicle, described as a 'mobile billboard,' displays 'Fora Lula' (Lula Out) slogans, the voting number, and a pixuleco image, exceeding legal limits for vehicle advertising. Lawyers argue the full wrap of a double-decker bus constitutes irregular campaign propaganda.

item.title: Falas de Lula já não atenuam dano político do caso Lulinha
item.description: Lula's statements can no longer contain the political damage caused by the Lulinha case, which has put corruption back at the center of the electoral debate. With the anti-corruption agenda gaining traction among voters, the president had to revisit the same repertoire used in the 2022 succession, when he admitted wrongdoing in a televised interview. The episode highlights the government's difficulty in shielding itself from scandals involving family members in an election year.

item.title: Pesquisa senador SP: veja números do levantamento RealTime Big Data
item.description: A RealTime Big Data poll released on August 24, 2026 shows a technical tie among four candidates in the São Paulo Senate race, within the two-percentage-point margin of error. Guilherme Derrite (PP) leads with 18%, followed by Simone Tebet (PSB) with 17%, André do Prado (PL) with 15%, and Marina Silva (Rede) with 14%. The survey interviewed 2,000 voters by phone between August 19 and 22 and was registered with the TSE under number SP-01347/2026.

item.title: Ao contrário de Bolsonaro, Lula não está protegendo o filho, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, stated during a UOL/Folha interview that President Lula is not protecting his son Fábio Luís Lula da Silva from Federal Police investigations. Haddad made a direct comparison with former president Jair Bolsonaro, implying that Bolsonaro acted differently by shielding his children from similar probes.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Ministro da Fazenda defende combater 'pejotização' para conter déficit da Previdência Social
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan defended combating 'pejotização' (hiring workers as contractors instead of formally employed) to reduce the Social Security deficit, proposing rules on the percentage of PJ workers allowed in companies. The proposal, which could be sent to Congress in a new Lula term, was articulated by Durigan as a representative of the president's re-election campaign. The topic is also supported by Labor Minister Luiz Marinho, who awaits the STF's ruling on the use of MEI for labor fraud.

item.title: Filha de Clezão, do 8 de janeiro, pede para fazer ‘visita humanitária’ a Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Ana Luiza Duarte da Cunha, daughter of Clezão — a January 8th detainee who died at the Papuda prison in 2023 — petitioned Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes for permission to make a 'humanitarian' visit to former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brasília. A candidate for district deputy running under the ballot name 'Luiza do Clezão,' she argues the meeting is part of her grieving process and pledges not to give interviews or post about it on social media. Bolsonaro is barred from receiving visitors, though Moraes has already authorized his sons Carlos and Jair Renan; Flávio Bolsonaro's visits remain suspended until October.

item.title: A Saúde nos programas de Caiado, Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The provided content contains only the institutional description of Observatório das Eleições, an academic initiative coordinated by UFMG and IEPI under professor Leonardo Avritzer, which monitors electoral issues since 2018. The text does not effectively present the health proposals from the programs of Caiado, Zema, and Flávio Bolsonaro, being limited to the editorial framing of the publication. A substantive analysis of these candidates' health platforms would require access to the actual article body.

item.title: Marqueteiro de Flávio, Duda Lima passará a acompanhar candidato em viagens após sugestão de aliados
item.description: Marketing strategist Duda Lima, the third to hold the role in Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, will shift from his São Paulo headquarters-based work to traveling with the candidate across Brazil, following allies' suggestion. The change comes as Flávio expands his agenda, including his first Northeast trip to Alagoas with vice-presidential candidate Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), where he faces difficulties with local allies like JHC and Arthur Lira. The goal is to adapt Flávio's communication and discourse to different regional scenarios, such as the Northeast, where Lula leads by 28 points in the latest Datafolha poll.

item.title: Filiação ao PRTB e União Brasil: O questionamento da Justiça Eleitoral sobre a campanha de Marçal
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Public Ministry questioned the validity of Pablo Marçal's affiliation with PRTB following public statements linking him to União Brasil. Brazilian electoral law requires candidates to have their party affiliation approved and registered with the Electoral Justice at least six months before the election date. The inconsistency between public declarations and official records could jeopardize Marçal's candidacy.

item.title: Fachin recebe Janja no STF para discutir ações de combate à violência contra a mulher
item.description: STF Chief Justice Edson Fachin met with First Lady Janja Lula da Silva to discuss measures to combat feminicide and gender violence as part of the 'Todas por Todas' (All for All) pact uniting the three branches of government. During the meeting, Fachin presented CNJ results, noting that 53% of emergency protective measures are granted on the same day they reach the courts. The meeting follows an STF ruling expanding the scope of protective measures under the Maria da Penha Law to gender-based violence outside the domestic sphere.

item.title: Por que Pablo Marçal pode ‘tumultuar’ a eleição e favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo cientista político
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares assesses that a potential presidential run by Pablo Marçal would have more potential to disrupt the race than to take him to a runoff. According to Tavares, Marçal's strength lies in his social media mobilization and ability to create political moments, but he faces difficulties with party structure, TV time, and coalition-building. This entry could fragment the right-wing field and, paradoxically, benefit Flávio Bolsonaro by reducing pressure on the senator.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo e ao Senado em Mato Grosso
item.description: The article presents the six candidates for governor of Mato Grosso and the ten contenders for Senate in the 2026 elections, including profiles of Natasha Slhessarenko (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicans), and Rafael Milas (Mission). Brasil Real Time polls show Wellington Fagundes leading the governor's race and Mauro Mendes and Janaína Riva ahead in the Senate contest. Voters will choose two names for the Federal Senate, along with president, governor, and legislators.

item.title: A iniciativa de movimentos sociais para pressionar votação da PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: The Frentes Brasil Popular and Povo Sem Medo have called for a mobilization on Sunday to pressure senators to vote on the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule. The Senate's CCJ is expected to hold a public hearing on Tuesday, September 1st, with rapporteur Omar Aziz presenting his opinion the following day. There are still doubts about whether there will be enough time for the proposition to advance before the October elections.

item.title: A postura do governo Lula diante da revelação de mais de mil mortes na terra Yanomami
item.description: Data from the Ministry of Health reveals 1,121 deaths of Yanomami indigenous people in Lula's first three years in office, surpassing the 951 deaths recorded during the Bolsonaro administration. The government reacted with indignation at the disclosure by Veja magazine rather than addressing the humanitarian crisis, according to Senator Damares Alves, chair of the Senate Human Rights Commission. Health Minister Alexandre Padilha recorded a video defending the administration and criticizing the publication, while the Presidency labeled the analyses as 'inaccurate,' appearing more concerned with electoral impact than with the causes of deaths from malnutrition, malaria, and respiratory diseases.

item.title: Quem ganhou e quem perdeu o primeiro debate presidencial, segundo cientista político
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares assessed the first presidential debate, highlighting that Romeu Zema's absence was damaging since the governor needs to increase his name recognition and has low polling numbers (2% to 3%). Meanwhile, Renan Santos leveraged the opportunity to produce strategic content for social media. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, being well-positioned in the race, had a strategic justification for their absence as they had more to lose than to gain.

item.title: “Estrelas da corrupção” estão na chapa de Gaspar, diz defesa de Lulinha
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva's (Lulinha's) lawyer, Marco Aurélio Carvalho, fired back at vice-presidential candidate Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), claiming the 'true stars of corruption' are Gaspar's running mates. Carvalho accused Gaspar of having '61 million reasons to stay quiet' and of already being a suspect in court, defended Lulinha as living in Spain on his own income, and denied any connection between Lula's son and Brazil's social security institute (INSS).

item.title: ‘Todos os prefeitos do PL estão engajados na nossa campanha’, comenta Ruas sobre 'traidores' do partido no Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL), candidate for Governor of Rio, stated during a rally in Praça Seca that all PL mayors are engaged in his campaign, rejecting the 'traitors' label. However, a GLOBO survey shows that nine of the 22 party mayors in the state had not publicly declared support for him. The rally was Ruas's first without Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: ‘Efeito Tarcísio’ impulsiona direita e embaralha corrida pelo Senado em São Paulo, mostra pesquisa
item.description: The 'Tarcísio effect' is strengthening right-wing candidates in the race for two Senate seats in São Paulo. Guilherme Derrite has taken the lead in the Real Time Big Data poll, surpassing Simone Tebet and Marina Silva, who had led previous surveys. However, Ricardo Salles' candidacy, with around 10% of voting intentions, could split the right-wing field and benefit opponents, according to political scientist Elias Tavares.

item.title: LULA grava ENTREVISTA para RECORD no ALVORADA: NÃO era PROIBIDO usar o ALVORADA em CAMPANHA?
item.description: The report questions the use of the Alvorada Palace as the setting for an exclusive interview with President Lula on Record TV, suggesting possible improper electoral use of public property. The content went viral on social media and sparked debate about the legality and ethics of using the official residence for campaign purposes. No further information about discussed policies or proposals is available.

item.title: João Azevêdo lidera disputa pelo Senado na PB, diz Real Time Big Data
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll released on August 24, 2026, shows that former Paraíba governor João Azevêdo (PSB) leads the race for one of the state's two Senate seats with 29% of mentions, followed by Senator Veneziano Vital do Rêgo (MDB) with 23%. The survey interviewed 1,600 voters in Paraíba between August 19 and 22, has a 95% confidence level and a margin of error of 2 percentage points, and was registered with Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) under number PB-07790/2026.

item.title: Lula sugere Desenrola para clubes e comenta intervenção no Corinthians
item.description: President Lula suggested to Caixa Econômica Federal the creation of a Desenrola program specifically for football clubs, claiming teams are 'broken' due to poor management and high salaries. He also did not oppose a possible judicial intervention at Corinthians, the team he supports, conditioning the measure to proof of necessity.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro alega sátira e pede que vídeo de Lulinha siga no ar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) legal team asked a São Paulo court to keep online an AI-generated video associating Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, with fraud against INSS retirees. The lawyers argued the content is political satire protected by free speech, noting Lulinha's name appeared in an official procedure tied to Operação Sem Desconto. Lulinha — son of President Lula, who is running for reelection — had sued to have the video removed and sought R$10,000 in moral damages.

item.title: Caso Lulinha já aparece na nova pesquisa sobre Lula x Flávio? Cientista político analisa a disputa
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares assesses that the revelations regarding suspicions of influence trafficking involving Lulinha, President Lula's son, represent a new risk factor for the government candidacy, but have not yet been captured by electoral polls. The race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remains within the margin of error, with strong polarization and no room for a third alternative. The closeness between the candidates means that small shifts and new political events could be decisive in the final outcome.
